exposure: Use of an absorbable adhesion barrier (oxidized regenerated cellulose) during the initial cesarean delivery
outcome: Presence and severity of intraperitoneal adhesions at subsequent cesarean delivery
Time from skin incision to newborn delivery
cohort: 2125 women who underwent two consecutive cesarean deliveries between 2011 and 2018
finding: Placement of an absorbable adhesion barrier during the initial cesarean delivery was associated with a reduction in intraperitoneal adhesions and shorter surgery duration during the subsequent cesarean delivery.
